status: Experiment 1 of 1 completed; budget respected (1 experiment, <1 hour compute).
hypothesis: H82-1 (rank 1): hanging-wall fault-damage collar at the 300 m DTI kernel scale. Blind normal-fault splays that never entered the USGS/INGENIOUS Quaternary fault catalogue cluster off mapped traces at roughly one kernel radius (100-400 m); the collar is zero on the mapped trace, peaks near 3 px (300 m), decays to zero by ~1.2 km, and is computed per holdout fold from visible faults only. Full hypothesis ranking in research/h82_hypotheses.md; preregistered at registry/preregistration_h82.json before any experiment.
mechanism: Damage-zone permeability and off-trace upflow around blind normal faults produce a spatial prior peaked at damage-zone scale beside catalogue traces. The official Tversky-style DTI (alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular kernel) credits a dot within 300 m of a hidden truth cell and penalises redundant mass, so a sparse kernel-scale collar matches the metric's native scale without re-predicting mapped faults (which the organiser fully penalises, thread 11516).
named_non_fault_mimicking_process: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan (1332 m) and Bonneville (1552/1552 m) wave-cut terrace risers, symmetric V-shaped ephemeral washes/arroyos, and road or canal cuts - linear off-trace alignments with no dislocation damage zone.
